payload.headline: Tesla holds 380.14 under resistance; margins and cash flow weak, still avoid

summary.thesis: Tesla's sales have gone flat and its margins and cash flow are shrinking, yet the share price sits near the top of its own 5-year valuation range.
summary.decision: Long-term avoid; swing wait, because the price is stuck in a range just under heavy resistance.
summary.act_at: Re-examine near 293.94 after the 2027-01-27 report; swing only above 404.4 or on a hold at 363.86–368.76

payload.happening: Tesla fell 1.18% to 380.14. That leaves it just under a resistance zone at 380.15–389.95, where sellers have stepped in 9 times, and all three moving averages (20, 50 and 200 days) are flat. No news has been reported since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Several numbers point to the business itself getting weaker. Sales in the latest quarter changed -0.17% from a year earlier, after 15.78% growth two quarters ago. Operating margin (the profit kept from each sales dollar before interest and tax) fell to 3.35% from 4.74%. Free cash flow (cash left after running the business and paying for investment) dropped to 3.3B over the last 12 months, from 6.8B. Inventory is up 15% while quarterly sales are up 0%. Unsold cars can force price cuts, which would put margins under more pressure. Each dollar invested now earns 5¢ a year, against 33¢ three years ago. Those are changes to demand, margins and cash. What is not at risk is the balance sheet: net cash is 37.5B and total liquidity is 45.4B, so funding is not a concern. The internal macro view of a tech downtrend with elevated fear only affects sentiment, not the business. Segment data is not available, so this note cannot say which product lines are driving the slowdown.

worth.text: The methods disagree badly, and the gap comes down to growth. A discounted cash flow (DCF) model values a company from the cash it is expected to produce. Starting from trailing free cash flow of 3.3B and a 9.9% discount rate, it gives 20.17 (bear), 24.93 (base) and 45.0 (bull). Even if growth starts at 30%, the value is 45.37. The filings-based risk check says today's price needs about 51% a year growth, while the company has delivered 3% a year over 3 years and 8% over the last 12 months. On Tesla's own history, the price-to-sales ratio (price divided by sales per share) gives 203.8 at its 20th percentile, 293.94 at the middle and 399.81 at its 80th percentile. Today's price-to-sales of 14.5 sits at the 73rd percentile of its 5-year range, and the trailing price-to-earnings ratio is 418.3. If operating margin falls to 2%, the DCF value is 27.91. My range uses the lower half of Tesla's own valuation history, because the cash-flow models cannot reach today's price under any growth they test.
worth.key_assumption: With flat quarterly sales and operating margin down to 3.35%, the market will value Tesla in the low-to-middle part of its 5-year price-to-sales range, not near the 399.81 top.

bull: The balance sheet is very strong: net cash is 37.5B and liquidity is 45.4B, which leaves room to keep investing through a slow patch.
Analysts' next-year EPS growth figure is 25%, and the DCF bull case using the highest growth input is 45.0, well above the base of 24.93.
Sales over the last 12 months still grew to 103.6B from 95.6B, and R&D spending is 8.56% of revenue, which keeps new products funded.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 3.3B from 6.8B, and the DCF base value is 24.93 against a price of 380.14.
Operating margin dropped to 3.35% from 4.74%, and inventory is up 15% while quarterly sales are up 0%, which raises the risk of price cuts.
The valuation is stretched: trailing price-to-earnings is 418.3 and price-to-sales of 14.5 sits at the 73rd percentile of its own 5-year range.

levels.what: Today's close. It is close to the own-history top of 399.81 and far above the DCF base of 24.93, so value offers no support at this price.
Bottom of the nearest support zone (363.86–368.76), where buyers have stepped in 4 times. A close below it points to the next zone at 349.24–354.14.
Middle of the own-history price-to-sales range. Re-examine at this price only if the 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74%.

longterm.why: Sales growth, margins, cash flow and returns on investment are all weakening while the price sits near the top of its own valuation history. The business grade is D and the internal committee call is Reduce.

swing.why: The price sits just under resistance at 380.15–389.95 (9 touches), the averages are flat and the trend is a range, so there is no clean setup. No trade until a close above 404.4, or until a pullback holds at 363.86–368.76.

decision.timing: No new long-term position before the 2027-01-27 report. Options price an 11.5% move by 2026-12-18 and a 20.2% move by 2027-02-19, which covers the report, and recent actual swings (72.9) have been bigger than what options imply (56.1).

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly sales growth from a year earlier back above 0%.
Trailing free cash flow recovers toward 6.8B from 3.3B, which would lift the cash base the DCF starts from.
A close above 404.4, the top of the second resistance zone, would end the range and change the swing call from wait.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid long-term and wait on the swing; with no new news, the close of 380.14 just under the 380.15–389.95 resistance zone confirmed it.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
